title: Make Memory edit mode compact and form-focused on narrow viewports
description:
Problem: the deeper `/memories` edit-mode review showed the selected-memory edit panel scrolling nearly 1,000 px inside a roughly 300 px viewport area. The search controls and results list remain visible above the form, while save/check/cancel, ID/title/status, confidence, tags, references, source links, and content compete for the limited detail pane.

Desired outcome: editing a memory should shift the interface into a focused form state where the user can review metadata, content, references, and source links without deep nested scrolling.

Scope:
- In scope: memory edit-mode responsive layout, result-list collapse/focus behavior, grouped metadata sections, source-link/reference editor density, save/check/cancel hierarchy, and dirty-state feedback.
- Out of scope: changing memory JSON schema, validation semantics, or search behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entering edit mode gives the form enough first-viewport space on narrow screens.
- Search/results controls can collapse or step aside without losing the selected memory context.
- Tags, references, conflicts, source links, and content are grouped with clear labels and reachable controls.
- Save, check, and cancel remain visible or predictably sticky without crowding metadata fields.

Validation:
- Capture `/memories` selected edit mode before/after at narrow and desktop widths.
- Run focused browser checks for edit, validation/check, save/cancel, tag edits, and source-link edits.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 continued live review: Memories edit mode kept search/results above a nested selected pane whose form scroll height was much larger than the visible area.
